Problem Statement

A digital library aims to provide personalised book recommendations to its readers based on their borrowing habits and membership type. Develop a Java program to model this system using two classes: Reader and RecommendationEngine.

The Reader class should store the Reader ID, Reader Name, Number of Books Borrowed, and Membership Type (Gold, Silver, or Regular) as private instance variables with appropriate public getter methods. Use a parameterized constructor to initialize all reader details.

Each membership type is assigned recommendation points as follows:

Membership Type | Recommendation Points
Gold | 30
Silver | 20
Regular | 10

The Recommendation Score for each reader is calculated using the formula:

Recommendation Score = (Number of Books Borrowed × 5) + Membership Points

To determine whether a reader is eligible for a premium recommendation, create a separate class named RecommendationEngine containing the following method:

boolean eligible(Reader r)

A reader qualifies for a premium recommendation if the Recommendation Score is greater than or equal to 80. The Reader class should contain a method named checkEligibility() that internally creates an object of the RecommendationEngine class and invokes the method using:

engine.eligible(this);

This checkEligibility() method should return the eligibility status obtained from the RecommendationEngine.

The program should read the details of multiple readers, store all Reader objects in an array, calculate the recommendation score for each reader, determine their eligibility for premium recommendations, and display the details of every reader along with the recommendation score and eligibility status.

Input Format

ReaderID

Name

BorrowedBooks

MembershipType

Output Format

ReaderID

Reader Name

Recommendation Score

Eligible or Not Eligible

Sample Input and Output

Input | Output
101; Arun Kumar; 12; Gold | Reader ID : 101; Reader Name : Arun Kumar Recommendation Score : 90; Eligible
